fullPassage:
Over the past two centuries, human activities have generated a significant amount of carbon dioxide, commonly referred to as CO2. This gas itself is not dangerous when we encounter it in everyday situations. However, excessive amounts of this gas in the atmosphere have contributed to the greenhouse effect, resulting in a gradual increase in the Earth's surface temperature. To make matters worse, this increase has sped up in recent years and is seriously threatening life on our planet. We must act immediately to stop any further climate change.

While many high-tech solutions such as carbon capture have been proposed, they are often too expensive to be used widely. Fortunately, there are also low-tech, economical, and even long-lasting solutions available. In this report, we will focus on one of the most powerful nature-based solutions to climate change: whales, the giant helpers living under the sea.

Whales are amazing creatures. They are enormous and live incredibly long lives. The largest blue whales can grow as long as 30 meters and weigh over 200 tons, and some whales have been known to live for more than 100 years. These giants do extremely beneficial things for the environment throughout their long lives and even after death. According to scientists, a single whale can absorb about 550 kilograms of CO2 per year, while a tree can absorb only 22.

Moreover, after they die, whales sink to the ocean floor with all the CO2 they absorbed during their lives. Their bodies then become food and habitats for deep-sea creatures. This process is called a whale fall. Whale falls permanently bury about 145,000 tons of CO2 under the sea every year. This achievement is basically what expensive carbon capture technologies aim to do — capture carbon and then store it underground.

In addition to their direct absorption and burial of CO2 through whale falls, whales also make a significant indirect contribution to reducing CO2 through an act called a whale pump. This refers to the vertical movements of whales that help circulate nutrients across different depths of the ocean. Whales dive deep into the ocean to feed on prey such as krill and small fish, and they occasionally swim up to the surface to breathe. When they near the surface, they release an enormous amount of waste. This waste is rich in nutrients that are essential for creatures living in that area. Specifically, it creates the perfect growing conditions for some microscopic creatures floating at the surface of the ocean.

These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look tiny and insignificant, but when taken together, they play a significant role in reducing CO2. They absorb about 40% of the carbon in the atmosphere and produce about 50% of the atmosphere's oxygen. They do this through photosynthesis, a process that creates energy using carbon, water, and light. It is estimated that increasing the world's phytoplankton by 1% is equivalent to planting 2 billion new trees. Whale pumps deliver nutrients not only to the ocean surface but also to deeper areas of the ocean. As whales swim back down to feed at the ocean's bottom, their movements stir up the water and bring nutrients down to the creatures living below. Whale pumps promote the growth of marine life at various depths throughout the ocean.

Whales spread nutrients in the ocean not only vertically but also horizontally through a process called the great whale conveyor belt. These giant mammals migrate over long distances at certain times of the year. For example, in the summer, humpback whales tend to stay near Alaska, where the water is cold but rich in nutrients and prey for them to feed on. As winter approaches, they travel up to 4,800 kilometers to breed in the warm waters near Hawaii.

Nutrients are relatively scarce in warm waters, which makes it difficult for phytoplankton to survive. Fortunately, when the whales arrive in Hawaii after eating their fill in Alaska, they release a large amount of nutrient-rich waste. This process can be thought of as a conveyor belt that moves nutrients from cold waters to warm waters. These nutrients support the life of many marine animals and, importantly, encourage the growth of phytoplankton even in warm waters. The spread of phytoplankton leads to increased carbon absorption throughout the entire ocean. Whales circulate water and nutrients to every corner of the ocean, helping to combat climate change.

Despite the important roles of whales in our environment, their lives are at serious risk. The number of whales had dramatically dropped until killing them for commercial purposes was officially banned in 1986. It is estimated that the global whale population fell from 4 to 5 million to just over 1 million during the decades before the ban. Today, whales are still threatened by various man-made dangers, such as fishing nets, ship strikes, and microplastic pollution in the ocean. It is important to recognize that whales are valuable partners in our fight against the climate crisis and that protecting them is an effective and cost-efficient way to address this global challenge. Let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives.

questions.passage: Over the past two centuries, human activities have generated a significant amount of carbon dioxide, commonly ①<u>referred</u> to as CO2. However, excessive amounts of this gas in the atmosphere have contributed to the greenhouse effect, ②<u>resulting</u> in a gradual increase in the Earth's surface temperature. To make matters worse, this increase has sped up in recent years and is seriously ③<u>threatening</u> life on our planet. We must act immediately ④<u>stop</u> any further climate change.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'to stop'인데 to가 빠졌다. 'act immediately to stop'에서 to부정사가 목적을 나타냄.
det.analysis:
✅ ① referred: commonly referred to as (과거분사 후치수식)
✅ ② resulting: 분사구문 (결과)
✅ ③ threatening: is seriously threatening (진행형)
❌ ④ stop → to stop: act immediately to stop (to부정사 목적)
det.tip: to부정사의 부사적 용법(목적): ~하기 위해. act to stop = 멈추기 위해 행동하다.

questions.passage: Whales dive deep into the ocean to feed on prey such as krill and small fish, and they occasionally swim up to the surface to breathe. When they near the surface, they release an enormous amount of waste. This waste is rich in nutrients ①<u>that</u> are essential for creatures living in that area. These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look tiny and insignificant, but when ②<u>taking</u> together, they play a significant role in reducing CO2. They absorb about 40% of the carbon in the atmosphere and ③<u>produce</u> about 50% of the atmosphere's oxygen. It is estimated that ④<u>increasing</u> the world's phytoplankton by 1% is equivalent to planting 2 billion new trees.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문은 'when taken together'이다. 주어(they=phytoplankton)가 '취해지는' 것이므로 과거분사 taken이 맞다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① that: 관계대명사 주격 (nutrients를 수식)
❌ ② taking → taken: 분사구문 수동. when (they are) taken together
✅ ③ produce: 주어 They에 대한 동사 (복수 일치)
✅ ④ increasing: 동명사 주어 (that절의 주어)
det.tip: 분사구문에서 주어가 동작의 대상이면 과거분사: when taken = when they are taken. take together = 합치다(수동).

questions.passage: Moreover, after they die, whales sink to the ocean floor with all the CO2 they ①<u>absorbed</u> during their lives. Their bodies then become food and habitats for deep-sea creatures. Whale falls permanently bury about 145,000 tons of CO2 under the sea every year. This achievement is basically ②<u>that</u> expensive carbon capture technologies aim to do. Nutrients are relatively scarce in warm waters, ③<u>which</u> makes it difficult for phytoplankton to survive. The number of whales had dramatically ④<u>dropped</u> until killing them for commercial purposes was officially banned in 1986.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문은 'what expensive carbon capture technologies aim to do'이다. what = the thing that. that으로는 aim to do의 목적어가 없어 불완전.
det.analysis:
✅ ① absorbed: 관계대명사 생략 (the CO2 (that) they absorbed)
❌ ② that → what: 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what 필요. 'is basically what ~ aim to do'
✅ ③ which: 계속적 용법 관계대명사 (앞 절 전체를 선행사로)
✅ ④ dropped: 과거완료 had dropped (1986년까지의 상황)
det.tip: what = the thing(s) that. 'This is what they aim to do.' aim to do의 목적어가 필요하므로 that이 아닌 what.

questions.passage: While many high-tech solutions such as carbon capture have been proposed, they are often too ①<u>expensive</u> to be used widely. Whales are amazing creatures. These giants do extremely ②<u>beneficial</u> things for the environment throughout their long lives and even after death. Whale falls permanently bury about 145,000 tons of CO2 under the sea every year. This achievement is basically what expensive carbon capture technologies aim to do — capture carbon and then ③<u>release</u> it underground. Despite the important roles of whales in our environment, their lives are at serious ④<u>risk</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문은 'store(저장하다)'인데 'release(방출하다)'로 바뀌었다. 탄소를 포집한 후 지하에 저장하는 것이지 방출하는 것이 아님.
det.analysis:
✅ ① expensive(비싼): 원문 일치
✅ ② beneficial(유익한): 원문 일치
❌ ③ release(방출하다) → store(저장하다): 반의어 교체. 탄소 포집의 목적은 저장
✅ ④ risk(위험): 원문 일치
det.tip: store(저장하다) ↔ release(방출하다). carbon capture = 탄소 포집 후 지하 저장이 목적.

questions.passage: In addition to their direct absorption and burial of CO2 through whale falls, whales also make a significant ①<u>abundant</u> contribution to reducing CO2 through an act called a whale pump. This refers to the vertical movements of whales that help ②<u>circulate</u> nutrients across different depths of the ocean. Nutrients are relatively scarce in warm waters, which makes it difficult for phytoplankton to survive. The spread of phytoplankton leads to increased carbon ③<u>absorption</u> throughout the entire ocean. Whales circulate water and nutrients to every corner of the ocean, helping to ④<u>combat</u> climate change.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① 원문은 'indirect(간접적인)'인데 'abundant(풍부한)'로 바뀌었다. 고래 추락을 통한 직접적 기여에 더해 간접적(indirect) 기여를 한다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
❌ ① abundant(풍부한) → indirect(간접적인): 'In addition to their direct ~ also make a significant indirect contribution' 직접+간접 대비 구조
✅ ② circulate(순환시키다): 원문 일치
✅ ③ absorption(흡수): 원문 일치
✅ ④ combat(대항하다): 원문 일치
det.tip: direct(직접적) ↔ indirect(간접적). 'In addition to direct ~ also indirect'의 대비 구조를 파악해야 함.

questions.passage: When they near the surface, they release an enormous amount of waste. This waste is rich in nutrients that are essential for creatures living in that area. Specifically, it creates the perfect growing conditions for some microscopic creatures floating at the surface of the ocean. These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look tiny and insignificant, but when taken together, they __________.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: can only survive in cold waters
play a significant role in reducing CO2
depend entirely on whale waste to survive

det.korean: 식물성 플랑크톤은 작고 하찮아 보이지만 합치면 CO2 감소에 중요한 역할을 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ play a significant role in reducing CO2: 원문 일치
❌ ① 해양 생태계에 해로운: 오히려 유익함
❌ ② 차가운 물에서만: 따뜻한 물에서도 고래 덕에 생존
❌ ④ 전적으로 의존: 고래 외에도 영양분 공급원 있음
det.tip: may look ~ but: ~처럼 보이지만 (역접). tiny and insignificant BUT play a significant role.

questions.passage: Whales spread nutrients in the ocean not only vertically but also horizontally through a process called the great whale conveyor belt. In the summer, humpback whales tend to stay near Alaska, where the water is cold but rich in nutrients. As winter approaches, they travel up to 4,800 kilometers to breed in the warm waters near Hawaii. When the whales arrive in Hawaii after eating their fill in Alaska, they release a large amount of nutrient-rich waste. This process can be thought of as __________.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: a conveyor belt that moves nutrients from cold waters to warm waters
a method to increase whale populations in tropical regions
a strategy whales use to avoid predators during migration
a natural process that cools down warm ocean waters

det.korean: 이 과정은 차가운 물에서 따뜻한 물로 영양분을 옮기는 컨베이어 벨트에 비유된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 차→따뜻한 물로 영양분 이동하는 컨베이어 벨트: 원문 일치
❌ ② 열대 지역 고래 수 증가: 맥락 없음
❌ ③ 포식자 회피 전략: 포식자 언급 없음
❌ ④ 따뜻한 바다 냉각: 수온 냉각 언급 없음
det.tip: conveyor belt(컨베이어 벨트) = 한 곳에서 다른 곳으로 물건을 옮기는 장치. 고래가 알래스카→하와이로 영양분을 운반.

questions.passage: Over the past two centuries, human activities have generated a significant amount of carbon dioxide, commonly referred to as CO2. This gas itself is not dangerous when we encounter it in everyday situations. However, excessive amounts of this gas in the atmosphere have contributed to the greenhouse effect, resulting in a gradual increase in the Earth's surface temperature. To make matters worse, this increase has sped up in recent years and is seriously threatening life on our planet. We must act immediately to stop any further climate change. While many high-tech solutions such as carbon capture have been proposed, they are often too expensive to be used widely. Fortunately, there are also low-tech, economical, and even long-lasting solutions available.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 한 마리의 고래는 연간 약 550kg의 CO2를 흡수할 수 있다.
나무 한 그루는 연간 약 550kg의 CO2를 흡수한다.

det.korean: ② 과학자들에 따르면 고래 한 마리는 연간 약 550kg의 CO2를 흡수할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 550kg CO2: 원문 일치
❌ ① 200톤 이상이지 100톤이 아님 (단, '100톤 이상'도 사실이긴 하나 원문 수치는 200톤 이상)
❌ ③ 나무는 22kg만 흡수
❌ ④ 100년 이상이지 50년이 아님
det.tip: 숫자 확인: whale 550kg vs tree 22kg. 고래가 나무보다 약 25배 더 많이 CO2 흡수.

questions.passage: Over the past two centuries, human activities have generated a significant amount of carbon dioxide, commonly referred to as CO2. This gas itself is not dangerous when we encounter it in everyday situations. However, excessive amounts of this gas in the atmosphere have contributed to the greenhouse effect, resulting in a gradual increase in the Earth's surface temperature. To make matters worse, this increase has sped up in recent years and is seriously threatening life on our planet. We must act immediately to stop any further climate change. While many high-tech solutions such as carbon capture have been proposed, they are often too expensive to be used widely. Fortunately, there are also low-tech, economical, and even long-lasting solutions available.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 금지 이전 수십 년간 고래 수가 급감했다.
오늘날 고래는 어망, 선박 충돌 등의 위협을 받고 있다.
금지 이후 고래 개체수가 500만 마리 이상으로 회복되었다.

det.korean: ④ 원문에는 금지 이후 개체수 회복에 대한 언급이 없다. 현재도 여전히 위협받고 있다고만 서술.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 1986년 금지: 원문 일치
✅ ② 금지 전 급감: 원문 일치
✅ ③ 어망, 선박 충돌 등: 원문 일치
❌ ④ 500만 이상 회복: 원문에 없음. 4~5백만→약 1백만으로 감소했다고만 함
det.tip: 내용일치 문제에서는 '원문에 없는 내용'도 오답이 될 수 있다. 회복 언급 없음.

questions.passage: These giant mammals migrate over long distances at certain times of the year. For example, in the summer, humpback whales tend to stay near Alaska, where the water is cold but rich in nutrients and prey for them to feed on. As winter approaches, they travel up to 4,800 kilometers to breed in the warm waters near Hawaii. Nutrients are relatively scarce in warm waters, which makes it difficult for phytoplankton to survive. Fortunately, when the whales arrive in Hawaii after eating their fill in Alaska, they release a large amount of nutrient-rich waste.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ③ 겨울이 다가오면 혹등고래는 최대 4,800km를 이동하여 하와이로 간다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 4,800km 이동: 원문 일치
❌ ① 여름에는 알래스카, 겨울에 하와이
❌ ② 따뜻한 물에는 영양분이 scarce(부족)
❌ ④ 하와이에서 번식(breed), 알래스카에서 먹이활동
det.tip: summer=Alaska(먹이), winter=Hawaii(번식). 이동 거리 최대 4,800km.

questions.passage: In addition to their direct absorption and burial of CO2 through whale falls, whales also make a significant indirect contribution to reducing CO2 through an act called a whale pump. This refers to the vertical movements of whales that help circulate nutrients across different depths of the ocean. When they near the surface, they release an enormous amount of waste. This waste is rich in nutrients that are essential for creatures living in that area. Specifically, it creates the perfect growing conditions for some microscopic creatures floating at the surface of the ocean.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 고래 펌프를 통한 고래의 간접적 CO2 감소 기여
고래가 깊은 바다에서 먹이를 찾는 방법
고래 배설물이 해양 오염에 미치는 영향

det.korean: 고래 펌프(whale pump)를 통해 영양분을 순환시키고 식물성 플랑크톤 성장을 도와 간접적으로 CO2를 줄이는 기여.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 고래 펌프를 통한 간접 CO2 감소: 핵심 주제
❌ ② 먹이 찾기 방법: 부분적 설명일 뿐
❌ ③ 수직 이동 패턴: 고래의 이동이 아닌 그 효과가 핵심
❌ ④ 해양 오염: 배설물은 오히려 유익함
det.tip: 주제 = 가장 포괄적인 내용. whale pump → nutrients → phytoplankton → CO2 감소 체인.

questions.passage: It is important to recognize that whales are valuable partners in our fight against the climate crisis and that protecting them is an effective and cost-efficient way to address this global challenge. Whales circulate water and nutrients to every corner of the ocean, helping to combat climate change. While many high-tech solutions such as carbon capture have been proposed, they are often too expensive to be used widely. Fortunately, there are also low-tech, economical, and even long-lasting solutions available.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 기후 위기 해결을 위해 첨단 기술에 더 많은 투자가 필요하다.
고래 보호는 기후 변화에 대응하는 효과적이고 경제적인 방법이다.
해양 생태계 보존보다 탄소 포집 기술 개발이 우선이다.

det.korean: 요지: 고래 보호는 기후 위기에 대응하는 효과적이고 비용 효율적인(cost-efficient) 방법이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 고래 보호 = effective + cost-efficient: 원문의 핵심 주장
❌ ① 첨단 기술 투자: 오히려 비싸서 wide하게 쓰기 어렵다고 함
❌ ③ 탄소 포집 우선: 자연 기반 해결책(고래)을 강조
❌ ④ 충분히 회복: 여전히 위협받고 있다고 함
det.tip: effective(효과적인) + cost-efficient(비용 효율적인) = 고래 보호가 기후 위기 해결의 저비용 고효율 해법.

questions.passage: These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look tiny and insignificant, but when taken together, they play a significant role in reducing CO2. They absorb about 40% of the carbon in the atmosphere and produce about 50% of the atmosphere's oxygen. It is estimated that increasing the world's phytoplankton by 1% is equivalent to <u>planting 2 billion new trees</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>planting 2 billion new trees</u>가 이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 실제로 20억 그루의 나무를 심어야 한다는 환경 캠페인
나무가 식물성 플랑크톤보다 더 효과적으로 CO2를 흡수한다는 사실
식물성 플랑크톤 1% 증가가 가져오는 CO2 감소 효과의 엄청난 규모
고래가 직접 나무를 대체하여 CO2를 흡수한다는 비유

det.korean: '20억 그루의 나무를 심는 것'은 식물성 플랑크톤 1% 증가의 탄소 흡수 효과가 얼마나 어마어마한지를 비유적으로 보여준다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 플랑크톤 1% 증가의 엄청난 규모: 20억 그루라는 숫자로 규모를 실감나게 비유
❌ ① 실제 나무 심기 캠페인: 비유일 뿐
❌ ② 나무가 더 효과적: 오히려 플랑크톤이 더 효과적임을 보여줌
❌ ④ 고래가 나무를 대체: 플랑크톤에 대한 비유이지 고래 자체가 아님
det.tip: is equivalent to = ~에 상당하다. 숫자(2 billion)를 통해 추상적 효과를 구체적으로 제시하는 수사법.

questions.passage: Moreover, after they die, whales sink to the ocean floor with all the CO2 they absorbed during their lives. Their bodies then become food and habitats for deep-sea creatures. This process is called a whale fall. Whale falls permanently bury about 145,000 tons of CO2 under the sea every year. This achievement is basically what expensive carbon capture technologies aim to do — capture carbon and then store <u>it</u> underground.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>it</u>이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: it = carbon. 'capture carbon and then store it underground'에서 it은 바로 앞의 carbon을 가리킴.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ carbon: capture carbon and store it = 탄소를 포집하고 저장하다
❌ ① whale fall: 과정(process)이지 저장 대상이 아님
❌ ② ocean floor: 해저는 저장 장소이지 대상이 아님
❌ ③ CO2: 바로 앞 문장의 carbon이 더 직접적 선행사
det.tip: 대명사 it의 선행사는 가장 가까운 명사를 먼저 확인: capture carbon → store it = carbon을 저장하다.

questions.passage: As winter approaches, they travel up to 4,800 kilometers to breed in the warm waters near Hawaii. Nutrients are relatively scarce in warm waters, which makes it difficult for phytoplankton to survive. Fortunately, when the whales arrive in Hawaii after eating their fill in Alaska, they release a large amount of nutrient-rich waste. This process can be thought of as a conveyor belt that moves nutrients from cold waters to warm waters. <u>These nutrients</u> support the life of many marine animals and, importantly, encourage the growth of phytoplankton even in warm waters.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>These nutrients</u>가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 고래가 하와이에서 배출한 영양분이 풍부한 배설물 속 영양분
따뜻한 바다에 원래 풍부하게 존재하는 영양분

det.korean: These nutrients = 고래가 하와이에 도착해 배출한 영양분이 풍부한 배설물 속 영양분. 컨베이어 벨트를 통해 전달된 영양분.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 고래 배설물 속 영양분: 직전 문장의 nutrients from cold to warm waters를 가리킴
❌ ② 따뜻한 바다 원래 영양분: scarce하다고 함
❌ ③ 알래스카 영양분: 이미 이동된 후의 영양분
❌ ④ 플랑크톤 생산 영양분: 플랑크톤은 영양분을 소비하는 쪽
det.tip: These nutrients는 직전 문장 'nutrients from cold waters to warm waters'를 받는 지시어.

questions.passage: These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look tiny and insignificant, but when taken together, they play a significant role in reducing CO2. They absorb about 40% of the carbon in the atmosphere and produce about 50% of the atmosphere's oxygen. They do this through __________, a process that creates energy using carbon, water, and light. It is estimated that increasing the world's phytoplankton by 1% is equivalent to planting 2 billion new trees. Whale pumps deliver nutrients not only to the ocean surface but also to deeper areas of the ocean. As whales swim back down to feed at the ocean's bottom, their movements stir up the water and bring nutrients down to the creatures living below. Whale pumps promote the growth of marine life at various depths throughout the ocean. Whales spread nutrients in the ocean not only vertically but also horizontally through a process called the great whale conveyor belt.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.
"식물성 플랑크톤은 (          )을 통해 탄소, 물, 빛을 사용하여 에너지를 만든다.". (1단어)

det.korean: 식물성 플랑크톤은 광합성(photosynthesis)을 통해 에너지를 만든다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'through photosynthesis, a process that creates energy using carbon, water, and light.' 빈칸은 photosynthesis.
det.tip: photosynthesis = 광합성. photo(빛) + synthesis(합성). 탄소 + 물 + 빛 → 에너지.

questions.passage: Whales spread nutrients in the ocean not only vertically but also __________ through a process called the great whale conveyor belt. These giant mammals migrate over long distances at certain times of the year. For example, in the summer, humpback whales tend to stay near Alaska, where the water is cold but rich in nutrients and prey for them to feed on. As winter approaches, they travel up to 4,800 kilometers to breed in the warm waters near Hawaii. Nutrients are relatively scarce in warm waters, which makes it difficult for phytoplankton to survive. Fortunately, when the whales arrive in Hawaii after eating their fill in Alaska, they release a large amount of nutrient-rich waste. This process can be thought of as a conveyor belt that moves nutrients from cold waters to warm waters. These nutrients support the life of many marine animals and, importantly, encourage the growth of phytoplankton even in warm waters.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.
"고래는 영양분을 수직으로뿐만 아니라 (          )으로도 퍼뜨린다.". (1단어)

det.korean: 고래는 영양분을 수직뿐 아니라 수평(horizontally)으로도 퍼뜨린다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'not only vertically but also horizontally.' 빈칸은 horizontally.
det.tip: vertically(수직으로) ↔ horizontally(수평으로). not only A but also B 구문.

questions.passage: It is important to recognize that whales are valuable partners in our fight against the climate crisis and that __________. Let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives.
questions.stem:
주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)
[ protecting / them / is / an / effective / and / cost-efficient / way / to / address / this / global / challenge ]. (13단어)
questions.wa: protecting them is an effective and cost-efficient way to address this global challenge
accept: protecting them is an effective and cost-efficient way to address this global challenge
Protecting them is an effective and cost-efficient way to address this global challenge
protecting them is an effective and cost-efficient way to address this global challenge.

det.korean: 그들을 보호하는 것은 이 글로벌 도전에 효과적이고 비용 효율적인 방법이다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'protecting them is an effective and cost-efficient way to address this global challenge.' 13단어 배열.
det.tip: protecting(동명사 주어) + is + an effective and cost-efficient way + to address(to부정사 형용사적 용법).

questions.ans: protecting them is an effective and cost-efficient way to address this global challenge

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.
"우리는 더 이상의 기후 변화를 멈추기 위해 즉시 행동해야 한다."
[조건] must / act / immediately / stop 을 사용할 것. (10단어)
questions.wa: We must act immediately to stop any further climate change.
accept: We must act immediately to stop any further climate change.
We must act immediately to stop any further climate change
we must act immediately to stop any further climate change
we must act immediately to stop any further climate change.

det.korean: 우리는 더 이상의 기후 변화를 멈추기 위해 즉시 행동해야 한다.
det.analysis: We must act immediately to stop any further climate change. must + 동사원형, to부정사(목적).
det.tip: must act = 행동해야 한다. to stop = 멈추기 위해. any further = 더 이상의.

questions.ans: We must act immediately to stop any further climate change.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.
"더 많은 고래가 더 오래 더 건강하게 살도록 행동합시다."
[조건] take action / help / whales / live 를 사용할 것. (12단어)
questions.wa: Let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives.
accept: Let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives.
Let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives
let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives
let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives.

det.korean: 더 많은 고래가 더 오래 더 건강하게 살도록 행동합시다.
det.analysis: Let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives. help + 목적어 + 동사원형.
det.tip: Let's = ~합시다. take action = 행동을 취하다. help + O + V(원형) = O가 V하도록 돕다.

questions.ans: Let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives.
